title: OLED Framebuffer and show()
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Run display.fill(0), text(), ellipse(), rect(), and show() one step at a time to see that drawing changes only the framebuffer in memory and show() copies it to the OLED screen.

learningObjectives: Explain that drawing calls change only the framebuffer in memory.
Explain that display.show() copies the whole framebuffer to the OLED screen in one step.
Predict what the screen shows when fill(0) or show() is left out or out of order.
prerequisites: Pixels and screen coordinates with (0, 0) at the top left
The OLED display and SSD1306 sections (Chapter 9)

controls.label: 1. fill(0), 2. text(), 3. ellipse(), 4. rect(), 5. show()
controls.purpose: Run one display call at a time.

controls.label: Run all in order
controls.purpose: Run the five calls 600 ms apart, highlighting each line.

controls.label: Loop mode: move the ellipse / Stop loop
controls.purpose: Each 500 ms pass clears, draws the ellipse 8 pixels further right, and shows.

controls.label: Skip fill(0) in loop mode
controls.purpose: Leave out fill(0) to see the smeared trail.

assumptions: The display is 128 x 64 pixels, 1 bit per pixel.
Text uses a public-domain 8 x 8 font.
limitations: show() is instant here; the real transfer over I2C or SPI takes a few milliseconds.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: One button per code line, side-by-side memory and screen panels, highlighted code, and a status line
keyQuestions: Why does the screen stay blank after display.text() runs?
What does display.fill(0) change, and what does it not change?
Why do old drawings pile up in a loop without fill(0)?
commonMisconceptions: Drawing calls change the screen right away.
show() must be called after every single drawing call.
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the screen after text() and before show().
Explain and fix the smeared trail in loop mode.
Debug a loop that calls show() before the drawing calls.
